findings.description: Critical: Auth was fixed in OpenAPI (every /usage/* route requires ApiKey and is principal-scoped) but the authoritative specs and proposal still require the opposite: usage-accounting Requirement "Usage Query Routes" and agent-coordinator Requirement "Usage Ledger HTTP Coverage" both still say GET /usage/* are unauthenticated "matching existing convention", and proposal.md still says "Writes require the API key; reads follow the existing GET convention." Implementers following the specs will ship open reads that reintroduce the exact principal-enumeration risk the OpenAPI fix closed.
findings.resolution: Rewrite usage-accounting, agent-coordinator, and proposal to match OpenAPI: every /usage/* route requires the API key; reads are principal-scoped (own rows unless a named profile grant allows cross-principal). Add scenarios for 401 on GET without a key and for principal scoping.

findings.description: Critical: The session_overhead fix is specified in usage-accounting (orchestrator agent_id=null usage MUST appear under a distinct session_overhead bucket; per-phase rows + session_overhead MUST equal /usage/summary) but OpenAPI GET /usage/by-phase only returns { rows: PhaseUsageRow[] }. PhaseUsageRow requires dispatch_id/intended_model/mismatch flags and cannot represent that bucket, so the field the spec requires has no response schema that can supply it — and generated clients cannot consume it.
findings.resolution: Extend the by-phase (and any related) response schema with an explicit session_overhead object (TokenTotals plus change_id), document how orphan agent_id=null usage is classified into it, and regenerate types.

findings.description: Critical: DispatchRecordUpsert was split into DispatchRecordCreate and DispatchRecordPatch, but POST /usage/dispatch still declares requestBody schema DispatchRecordPatch only. DispatchRecordCreate is unused. A create body of {"dispatch_id":"d1"} validates against the wire contract yet cannot satisfy DB NOT NULL columns (change_id, phase, intended_model, session_id) or the event schema's stored-row required set — the split's whole point is not enforced on the route.
findings.resolution: Change POST /usage/dispatch to oneOf [DispatchRecordCreate, DispatchRecordPatch] (or separate create/patch operations), reject underspecified creates with 422, and regenerate generated/models.py which still exposes the obsolete DispatchRecordUpsert.

findings.description: Critical: The record_kind fix is wired to the wrong producer. Task 4.4a sets state_only for INIT/SUBMIT_PR inside build_phase_dispatch_kwargs, but those phases (and PLAN) go through record_state_only_archetype / runner record-state-only-archetype and never call build_phase_dispatch_kwargs. skill-workflow requires state-only phases to write a dispatch record with record_kind=state_only, yet no task updates record_state_only_archetype to POST that record. Result: either state-only rows are never written, or they are only written if someone mistakenly routes them through the dispatch helper — and PLAN is state_only in skill-workflow but omitted from task 4.4a / DB comments / the mismatches scenario (INIT+SUBMIT_PR only).
findings.resolution: Add an explicit task for record_state_only_archetype (INIT, PLAN, SUBMIT_PR) to POST DispatchRecordCreate with record_kind=state_only; keep build_phase_dispatch_kwargs at record_kind=dispatched only; align DB comments, usage-accounting scenarios, and skill-workflow on the same state_only phase set.

findings.description: Critical: After the non-Claude agent_id fix, the (session_id, agent_id) join still cannot be satisfied from the stated producers. D2/spec join on (session_id, agent_id); dispatch.session_id is the orchestrator session; sidechain discovery only requires stamping agent_id and parent_session_id (not forcing usage.session_id = parent/orchestrator); non-Claude usage naturally uses the vendor session as session_id while agent_id is also set to that vendor session id. Nothing requires usage.session_id == dispatch.session_id, so Claude sidechains and all non-Claude vendors remain systematically unattributed despite the agent_id patch.
findings.resolution: Normatively define join-key population: for sidechains, usage.session_id SHALL equal the orchestrator/parent session (parent_session_id) with agent_id = sub-agent id; for non-Claude, either dispatch.session_id SHALL be the vendor session shared with usage.session_id, or the join key SHALL be redefined (e.g. agent_id-only for non-Claude) with matching adapter and dispatch tasks/tests.

findings.description: Critical: Task 4.4c (exclude record_kind=state_only from /usage/mismatches, plus the zero-mismatch test) lives under Phase 4 / wp-dispatch, but the behavior is implemented in coordinator usage_ledger query code. wp-dispatch write scope denies agent-coordinator/src/**, so the package cannot legally implement or verify the exclusion it owns.
findings.resolution: Move 4.4c into wp-coordinator (tasks 3.5/3.6/3.7) or add a coordinator task that wp-dispatch depends on; keep wp-dispatch limited to emitting record_kind correctly.

findings.description: Critical: limit/cursor were added to GET /usage/summary, /by-phase, /by-model, and /mismatches, but only /usage/events returns next_cursor. Aggregate response schemas have no pagination envelope, and UsageSummary is a single totals object — what limit/cursor truncates is undefined. Clients cannot page mature forever-retained ledgers despite the parameters the pagination fix advertised.
findings.resolution: Add next_cursor (and stable sort order) to every paginated aggregate response; define whether summary paginates by_model/by_vendor slices or is unpaged; align usage-accounting route requirements with the OpenAPI pagination contract.

findings.description: Nit: Principal server-derivation was marked readOnly on OpenAPI UsageRecord, but contracts/events/usage-record.schema.json still lists principal as a normal client-supplied property (additionalProperties:false inventory), and generated/models.py still accepts principal on ingest. Collectors following the event schema will keep sending a field the server must ignore/overwrite, and the three contracts disagree on who owns the value.
findings.resolution: Remove principal from the client event schema (or mark it explicitly server-only / not part of the wire payload), drop it from the generated ingest model input, and state that IngestBatch.host (or server context) is copied onto usage_records.host.

findings.description: Nit: usage-accounting requires each usage record to carry host, the event schema and DB column include host, and the cloud-parity scenario asserts host on stored records — but OpenAPI UsageRecord has no host property (host exists only on IngestBatch). The producer contract that must supply per-row host cannot do so through the OpenAPI ingest item schema, and no requirement says the server copies batch.host onto each row.
findings.resolution: Either add host to OpenAPI UsageRecord, or specify that the coordinator stamps usage_records.host from IngestBatch.host (and update the event schema if host is not client-sent per record).

findings.description: Nit: OpenAPI states reads are principal-scoped unless the caller's profile grants cross-principal visibility, but no delta spec defines that grant, which profile operation enables it, or a test scenario. agent-metrics --usage also has no requirement to present the API key now required by every GET /usage/* route, so the report package can implement against an auth model the contracts no longer allow.
findings.resolution: Add usage-accounting/agent-coordinator requirements for principal scoping and the cross-principal profile grant; update harness-engineering --usage to require coordinator auth headers and to degrade on 401.

findings.description: Nit: db/schema.sql documents that the retention job SHALL purge usage_ingest_state rows older than USAGE_INGEST_STATE_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30), but usage-accounting, agent-coordinator, design D6, and tasks 3.9/3.10 only require purging transcript_events. Cloud ephemeral hosts will accumulate orphan cursor rows with no implementing requirement.
findings.resolution: Either add ingest-state retention to the WatchdogService requirement and tasks 3.9/3.10, or remove the SHALL from the DB contract comments so implementers are not bound by an orphan rule.

findings.description: Nit: OpenAPI DispatchRecord (response) is allOf DispatchRecordPatch + timestamps, so it omits record_kind; the event schema and DB both persist record_kind. Clients reading POST /usage/dispatch responses cannot observe the field that mismatch accounting depends on. OpenAPI phase is also an unconstrained string while the event schema enums NON_TERMINAL_PHASES.
findings.resolution: Give DispatchRecord its own stored-row schema including record_kind (and create required fields), and constrain phase on Create/Patch to the same enum as dispatch-record.schema.json.

findings.description: Nit: agent-coordinator migration scenario still says "GIVEN a coordinator database at migration 034" then "migration 037 SHALL apply", left stale by the 035→037 renumber after 035 landed. Current tree already has 035_audit_log_delegated_from.sql, so the scenario's baseline is wrong.
findings.resolution: Retarget the scenario to the latest applied migration before 037 (or "N-1") so VALIDATE does not assume a 034-only database.

findings.description: Optional: dispatch-record.schema.json record_kind description refers to "'judge' records that run in-process" as needing exclusion, but the enum is only dispatched|state_only and skill-workflow/GATEKEEPER treat the gatekeeper as a real sub-agent dispatch. The prose invents a third kind the schema cannot represent.
findings.resolution: Drop the 'judge' wording, or add an explicit third record_kind if any in-process judge truly writes a dispatch row with null agent_id.

findings.description: The Create/Patch split, server-side record_hash recompute, estimated IS TRUE provenance check, and NON_TERMINAL_PHASES-aligned phase enum are coherent load-bearing fixes when taken in isolation — the residual risk is incomplete propagation into specs, route wiring, tasks, and join-key producers rather than the design intent of those fixes themselves.
findings.resolution: Keep those design choices; close the propagation gaps named in findings 1–7 before implementation.
